title: zip()
summary: Iterate several sequences in parallel, yielding tuples.
description: Stops at the shortest input — silently, unless `strict=True` (Python 3.10+), which raises on a length mismatch.

parameters.name: strict
parameters.description: Raise ValueError if the lengths differ.

examples.title: Pairing two lists
examples.code: for name, score in zip(['a', 'b'], [90, 80]):\n    print(name, score)

examples.title: Catching a mismatch
examples.output: ValueError: zip() argument 2 is shorter than argument 1

real_world_usage: Pairing headers with values, combining parallel result sets, transposing rows and columns with `zip(*rows)`.

common_mistakes.fix: Pass strict=True when the lengths are supposed to match.
It is an iterator: once consumed it is empty. Wrap in list() to reuse.
